title: Agentforce Service Consultant
description: Formerly Service Cloud Consultant. Case management, entitlements and SLAs, Knowledge, channels and Omni-Channel, AI agents for service, contact center analytics and integrations.

questions.prompt: What does first contact resolution (FCR) measure?

options.text: How quickly an agent picks up a new chat or call after it is routed to them
The number of cases each customer opens per month
The share of issues solved in the customer's first interaction
The time from case creation to the first agent reply

questions.explanation: FCR is the percentage of issues resolved without the customer having to come back. Time to first reply is a separate responsiveness metric.

questions.prompt: A contact center pushes agents to cut average handle time (AHT) aggressively. What risk should the consultant raise?

options.text: Rushed interactions lower resolution rates and bring repeat contacts
Shorter calls always raise customer satisfaction scores
AHT only applies to email, not phone or chat
AHT can't be measured for chat or messaging, so the reports will be incomplete

questions.explanation: Optimising AHT alone can push agents to close contacts before the issue is solved, which hurts FCR and satisfaction. Balance it with quality metrics.

questions.prompt: What is case deflection?

options.text: Closing duplicate cases automatically when they arrive
Customers solving their issue through self-service instead of a case
Transferring a call to another agent with more skills
Reassigning a case to a different queue after triage finds the wrong team has it

questions.explanation: Deflection means the customer finds the answer (for example in a knowledge article or from an AI agent) so no case is needed. It's measured as cases avoided.

questions.prompt: Which metric captures how customers felt about a specific support interaction?

options.text: Average speed of answer for that interaction
CSAT from a post-interaction survey
The size of the case backlog that day
Agent utilisation during the interaction

questions.explanation: CSAT asks the customer directly after the interaction. Speed, backlog and utilisation are operational measures.

questions.prompt: Customers complain about long waits before an agent joins a chat. Which metric tracks this?

options.text: Average speed of answer
Average handle time
Net promoter score
First contact resolution

questions.explanation: Average speed of answer measures how long customers wait before an agent picks up. AHT measures the length of the interaction itself.

questions.prompt: A client wants to cut support costs by 40% in three months by replacing agents with an AI agent. What should the consultant do?

options.text: Explain the risks, start with simple high-volume requests and measure
Refuse to involve AI in the service process at all
Commit to the 40% target in the contract to win the project
Agree, and switch every channel to the AI agent on day one to hit the target

questions.explanation: A consultant should set realistic expectations: start with well-understood, repeatable requests, keep a path to humans, and grow based on measured results.

questions.prompt: Why do contact centers adopt Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS)?

options.text: Agents capture and improve knowledge as they solve cases, so it gets reused
It is required before Omni-Channel can be enabled
It removes the need for a Case object because every question is answered by an article
It replaces agents with a library of articles

questions.explanation: KCS makes knowledge creation part of solving cases. Reusable answers speed up resolution and feed self-service.

questions.prompt: A company moving 600 agents to Service Cloud wants to minimise disruption. What rollout approach should the consultant recommend?

options.text: Let each team design its own console layout
Pilot with one team, then roll out in waves
Switch all 600 agents over on the same day
Run both systems in parallel with no end date

questions.explanation: A pilot proves the design with real work, and waves let support and training scale. Indefinite parallel running doubles the agents' work.

questions.prompt: How should agent training for a new Service Console be designed?

options.text: A slide deck emailed to every agent before go-live
Hands-on scenarios based on real cases in a sandbox
Training for team leads only, who brief their teams
Links to the documentation pinned on the home page

questions.explanation: Agents learn the console fastest by working realistic cases in a safe environment. Passive material is quickly forgotten.

questions.prompt: When migrating historical cases, what must be loaded first?

options.text: Case comments, email messages and their attachments
Accounts and contacts the cases relate to
Published Knowledge articles
Omni-Channel presence statuses

questions.explanation: Cases reference accounts and contacts, so parents must exist first (and users for ownership). Comments and attachments come after their cases.

questions.prompt: The org will hold 50 million cases. What should the design account for?

options.text: Turn off reporting on Case so queries stay fast
Nothing special, because Salesforce handles every data volume the same way automatically
Selective queries, indexing where needed, avoiding skew and an archiving plan
Put all cases under one account to keep the sharing simple

questions.explanation: At large volumes, query selectivity, indexing, avoiding data skew and archiving keep the org performing. Concentrating cases under one account causes skew.

questions.prompt: Who should own the definition of case statuses and reasons across regions?

options.text: A data governance group that agrees shared definitions
The integration team, since it loads most of the data
Each agent, choosing values that suit their own work
Whoever creates the picklist values first

questions.explanation: Shared definitions make reporting consistent across teams. Governance assigns ownership and controls changes.

questions.prompt: Where should routing and entitlement changes be tested before they reach agents?

options.text: In a sandbox, with test cases covering each routing path
Directly in production during the quietest hours
In an unrelated Developer Edition org with no data
Nowhere, because declarative changes don't need testing

questions.explanation: Routing and SLA logic affects every case, so test it in a sandbox with realistic scenarios. Declarative doesn't mean risk-free.

questions.prompt: After go-live, how can the team tell whether agents are actually using Knowledge?

options.text: Count how many articles were created in the first week
Check how many Knowledge licences are assigned
Report on articles attached to cases and agents' article views
Ask the team managers for their impression of usage

questions.explanation: Attach rates and views show real use in case work. License counts and impressions don't.

questions.prompt: Agents juggle several cases at once and need related records open side by side. What should be configured?

options.text: A separate page layout for each case an agent opens
A Service Console app with workspace tabs and subtabs
A home page dashboard listing the agent's open cases
A standard navigation app with one tab per object

questions.explanation: Console apps open records as workspace tabs with related records as subtabs, and add a utility bar for tools like history and macros.

questions.prompt: Case fields should appear only when relevant, for example Return Reason only when Type is Return. What should be used?

options.text: A separate record type and page layout for every case type, assigned by a flow
Dynamic Forms with field visibility rules
A validation rule that requires Return Reason for returns
A formula field that shows the return reason when needed

questions.explanation: Dynamic Forms show or hide fields and sections based on conditions, without multiplying record types and layouts.

questions.prompt: Agents repeat the same steps for password-reset cases: send a template email, set the status and close. What saves the most time?

options.text: A macro that performs the steps in one click
A dashboard of open password-reset cases
Quick Text that inserts the email body only
A new case record type for password resets

questions.explanation: Macros automate multi-step console actions such as sending an email and updating fields. Quick Text only inserts text.

questions.prompt: Complex cases need a technical specialist and a billing specialist with edit access alongside the owner. What fits?

options.text: A Public Read/Write org-wide default for cases
A public group with edit access to every case
Change the case owner back and forth between specialists
Case Teams with predefined team roles

questions.explanation: Case Teams give named people access to a case with defined roles while ownership stays with one agent.

questions.prompt: Customer users on a high-volume Experience Cloud site must see only cases for their own account. What grants this?

options.text: A sharing set that matches the user's account to the case's account
A criteria-based sharing rule for each customer account
The role hierarchy, with a customer role for each account that shares cases upward
A Public Read Only org-wide default for cases

questions.explanation: High-volume customer users have no roles, so sharing sets grant access based on matching lookups such as account.

questions.prompt: A healthcare client must encrypt patient details at rest while keeping them searchable for agents. What should be considered?

options.text: Classic encrypted text fields for every patient field
Store the data in a text file attached to the record
Classic encrypted text fields for every patient field, masked for all users
Shield Platform Encryption, choosing a scheme that supports search

questions.explanation: Shield Platform Encryption encrypts data at rest; deterministic encryption supports filtering, and some features behave differently with encrypted fields. Hiding fields isn't encryption.

questions.prompt: Agents must not see customers' full card numbers, but the billing team must. What enforces this?

options.text: A validation rule that blocks agents from editing it
A note in the console asking agents not to look
Remove the field from the agents' page layout
Field-level security through permission sets

questions.explanation: Field-level security controls visibility everywhere (reports, list views, API). Page layouts only affect the record page.

questions.prompt: A client asks for a custom 'Ticket' object instead of Case. What should the consultant advise?

options.text: Use Case, which already has routing, SLAs and channel features
Build a Ticket object, because custom objects are more flexible and have fewer limits
Rename the Opportunity object to Ticket and reuse it
Build both Ticket and Case and keep them in sync

questions.explanation: Case is built into Omni-Channel, email-to-case, entitlements, Knowledge and service reports. A custom object would need all of that rebuilt.

questions.prompt: Customers should be able to check the status of their cases and read answers without calling. What should the design include?

options.text: An Experience Cloud help center with case visibility and Knowledge
A public link to a case status report
A phone menu that reads the case status aloud
An automated email to each customer every hour with the status of every case they have

questions.explanation: A self-service portal combines case tracking and knowledge, cutting calls for status updates.

questions.prompt: What is the standard lifecycle of a Lightning Knowledge article?

options.text: New, then Assigned, then Resolved, by an owner
Private, then Public, then Deleted after a year
Draft, then Published, then Archived
Open, then Pending, then Closed, like a case

questions.explanation: Articles are drafted, published, and later archived. Editing a published article creates a new draft version, and the published version stays live until the new one is published.

questions.prompt: Partners should see installation articles, while customers see only troubleshooting articles. What controls this?

options.text: Article titles prefixed with 'Internal' or 'Partner'
A separate Knowledge org for partners and another for customers, synced nightly
Data categories with category visibility settings
Case record types linked to each article

questions.explanation: Data categories classify articles, and category group visibility controls who sees which categories. Channels decide where an article appears.

questions.prompt: An article must appear to agents and on the customer help center, but not to partners. What should be set?

options.text: The article's channels: internal app and customer
The article's validation status, set to Validated
The article's record type, set to Customer
A sharing rule on the Knowledge object

questions.explanation: Article channels (internal app, customer, partner, public knowledge base) control where an article is available.

questions.prompt: In KCS, what are the two loops?

options.text: The Solve loop and the Evolve loop
The Draft loop for writing and the Publish loop for review
The Inbound loop for calls and the Outbound loop for email
The Sales loop for revenue and the Service loop for cases

questions.explanation: The Solve loop happens during case work; the Evolve loop improves the knowledge base and process over time.

questions.prompt: Agents should be able to write an article from a case they just solved, with the case details pre-filled. What supports this?

options.text: Running a report of solved cases at the end of each week
Copying the case text into a new article in another browser tab and saving it
Creating the article from the case, with case fields mapped into it
Emailing the case details to the Knowledge team

questions.explanation: Agents can create an article from the case, with case fields mapped into the draft. This makes capture part of the workflow, which is central to KCS.

questions.prompt: Articles written by agents must be reviewed before customers can see them. What supports this?

options.text: Hiding draft articles in the Service Console
An approval process on Knowledge, with validation status
Publishing every article straight to all channels and fixing problems afterwards
A separate customer org for reviewed articles

questions.explanation: Knowledge supports approval processes and a validation status, so drafts are checked before publishing to external channels.

questions.prompt: An Agentforce service agent should answer questions using the company's published articles. What does the agent need?

options.text: Access to archived articles only, which never change
Knowledge as a grounding source for the agent
A separate Knowledge licence for each customer
A copy of every article pasted into the agent's topic instructions and kept updated

questions.explanation: The agent retrieves relevant published articles to ground its answers. Pasting content into instructions doesn't scale and goes out of date.

questions.prompt: Customers email support@company.com. Emails must become cases, and replies must stay on the same case. What should be configured?

options.text: An auto-response rule with no other setup
Email-to-Case with email threading
Web-to-Lead with an assignment rule
Web-to-Case with an email form on the website

questions.explanation: Email-to-Case creates cases from inbound email, and threading matches replies to the existing case instead of creating new ones.

questions.prompt: A company expects 8,000 web form submissions a day. What should the consultant check about Web-to-Case?

options.text: That Web-to-Case only works when customers are Person Accounts with portal access
That it requires a Knowledge licence for every visitor
Its daily limit of 5,000 cases; extra requests are queued
Nothing, because Web-to-Case has no daily limit

questions.explanation: Web-to-Case creates up to 5,000 cases in 24 hours; extra requests are queued. At higher volumes consider an API-based form or another channel.

questions.prompt: A company wants persistent, asynchronous conversations on its website and in its mobile app, which customers can pick up later. What fits?

options.text: Email-to-Case with a website link
Web-to-Case with a contact form
Legacy Chat with a pre-chat form
Messaging for In-App and Web

questions.explanation: Messaging for In-App and Web supports asynchronous, persistent conversations and is the successor to legacy Chat.

questions.prompt: Customers in Brazil prefer WhatsApp. What lets agents answer them from the Service Console?

options.text: Web-to-Case with a WhatsApp link on the form
An enhanced WhatsApp messaging channel
Email-to-Case with WhatsApp messages forwarded by email
A social listening tool with no reply capability

questions.explanation: Enhanced messaging channels bring WhatsApp, SMS and Facebook Messenger into the console, routed through Omni-Channel.

questions.prompt: A client wants phone calls inside the console with call transcripts and Omni-Channel routing. What should be recommended?

options.text: Service Cloud Voice
A softphone that runs outside Salesforce
Email-to-Case with voicemail sent as attachments
Open CTI on its own, with no Omni-Channel routing

questions.explanation: Service Cloud Voice integrates telephony with the console, Omni-Channel and real-time transcription.

questions.prompt: An Agentforce service agent can't solve a customer's issue. What should the design provide?

options.text: A hand-off to a human through Omni-Channel, with the transcript
End the conversation politely and suggest the customer tries again later today
Ask the customer to send an email to the support address
Restart the conversation from the beginning

questions.explanation: Service agents should hand off to humans when needed, routed through Omni-Channel so the agent sees the transcript.

questions.prompt: Which request is the best first candidate for an Agentforce service agent?

options.text: Approving a large refund outside policy
Order status checks that follow a well-defined lookup
Handling a complaint about a bereavement
Negotiating the settlement of a legal dispute with a customer

questions.explanation: High-volume, repeatable requests with clear data sources suit AI agents. Sensitive, judgement-heavy or high-risk cases should stay with people.

questions.prompt: What defines the jobs an Agentforce service agent can do, such as 'track an order' or 'reset a password'?

options.text: Queues that the agent can take work from
Topics, with instructions and actions
Case record types, one for each job the agent is allowed to do
Omni-Channel routing configurations

questions.explanation: Topics group what the agent handles, with instructions and actions (such as flows or Apex) it can call. The reasoning engine picks the topic from the customer's request.

questions.prompt: New cases about billing must go to the Billing queue; others to General Support. What is the simplest standard solution?

options.text: Escalation rules on new cases
Case assignment rules
Auto-response rules by case type
Sharing rules on the Billing queue

questions.explanation: Assignment rules route new cases to users or queues by criteria. Escalation rules act on cases that aren't resolved in time.

questions.prompt: High-priority cases still open after 4 business hours must be reassigned to a supervisor. What should be used?

options.text: An escalation rule with business hours
A dashboard alert sent to the supervisor
A validation rule on high-priority cases
A case assignment rule with a time condition

questions.explanation: Escalation rules act on cases left unresolved for a set time, respecting business hours, and can reassign and notify.

questions.prompt: Premium customers must get a first response within 1 hour and resolution within 8 hours. What should be configured?

options.text: An entitlement process with two milestones
Two escalation rules, one for the first response and one for resolution
A Premium case record type with its own layout
A formula field that counts the hours since creation

questions.explanation: Entitlement processes apply milestones with time limits and actions (warning, violation, success). The entitlement on the account or contact decides which process a case gets.

questions.prompt: A manager wants an alert 15 minutes before a First Response milestone is breached. Where is this set?

options.text: A case assignment rule with a 45-minute condition on high-priority cases
The case page layout's highlights panel
Warning actions on the milestone
An auto-response rule on the case

questions.explanation: Milestones have success, warning and violation actions. Warning actions fire before the deadline.

questions.prompt: SLAs must only count support hours (9 to 5, weekdays) and skip public holidays. What is needed?

options.text: A scheduled flow that pauses the timers each night
A scheduled flow that pauses every milestone timer at night and on holidays
Nothing, because milestones skip weekends automatically
Business hours with holidays, used by the entitlement process

questions.explanation: Business hours and holidays make milestone timers count only working time.

questions.prompt: Customers should get an email confirming their case number right after submitting a web form. What does this?

options.text: An escalation rule with an email action
Omni-Channel with a routing configuration
A case assignment rule with an email template
An auto-response rule

questions.explanation: Auto-response rules send a template email to the customer when a case is created from Web-to-Case or Email-to-Case.

questions.prompt: A customer emailed three times about the same issue and now has three cases. What should the agent do?

options.text: Transfer each case to a different agent
Delete the two newer cases
Merge the cases into one master case
Close two cases as duplicates without linking them

questions.explanation: Case merge combines up to three cases, keeping related records such as emails on the master case.

questions.prompt: An outage creates hundreds of similar cases. Agents need to update them together. What helps?

options.text: Ask customers to close their own cases
Merge all of the cases into one case
Relate them to a parent case
Create a separate queue for each outage case so they can be worked together

questions.explanation: A parent case (case hierarchy) groups related cases for coordinated updates. Merge works on small sets of true duplicates.

questions.prompt: Supervisors need a real-time view of which agents are online, their workload and waiting work. What provides this?

options.text: Omni-Channel Supervisor
A daily reporting snapshot of the queues
A list view of open cases by owner
A weekly dashboard of agent activity

questions.explanation: Omni Supervisor shows agent status, capacity and queue backlogs in real time. Reports and snapshots aren't real-time.

questions.prompt: Management wants to see how the open-case backlog changed over the past six months. What should be set up?

options.text: A list view of open cases sorted by age
A reporting snapshot that stores the backlog count each day
Field history tracking on the case Status field
A report on today's open cases, run every morning and saved by the manager

questions.explanation: Reporting snapshots save report results on a schedule into a custom object, so trends over time can be charted.

questions.prompt: Executives want trends, while team leads want each agent's open cases. How should dashboards be designed?

options.text: A separate dashboard built for each individual agent
One dashboard with every metric, so every audience sees the same numbers
Separate dashboards per audience, dynamic for team leads
A spreadsheet emailed to each audience every week

questions.explanation: Design for each audience's decisions. Dynamic dashboards run as the viewer, so one dashboard serves every team lead.

questions.prompt: How can a manager report on the share of cases that breached their resolution SLA?

options.text: Count cases where Priority is High and the case is older than one day
A report on Knowledge article views
Use only the case's Age field
Report on case milestones and whether they were violated

questions.explanation: Case milestone records track completion and violation, so they're the source for SLA compliance.

questions.prompt: How can CSAT survey results be reported alongside case data?

options.text: An email asking customers to reply with a score
A follow-up phone call from the team supervisor
Salesforce Feedback Management surveys linked to the case
A free-text field the agent fills in after each case

questions.explanation: Surveys sent after case closure can store responses linked to the case, so CSAT can be reported by agent, queue or case type.

questions.prompt: Which data source gives handle times for Omni-Channel routed work?

options.text: Agent Work records
Knowledge article versions
Case comment records
User login history records

questions.explanation: Agent Work records capture when work was assigned, accepted and closed, including handle time.

questions.prompt: A report must show cases together with their milestones. What is required?

options.text: Two separate reports combined in a spreadsheet
A report type that includes Cases with Milestones
A formula field on Case for each milestone
A dashboard filter on the case report

questions.explanation: Report types decide which related objects are available. Cases with milestones is a standard combination.

questions.prompt: How can deflection on the help center be measured?

options.text: Track help-center sessions that ended without a case
Count article drafts created by agents
Track the number of agent logins per day
Count every case closed in the period and compare it with last month's total

questions.explanation: Deflection is measured from customer journeys that ended in self-service instead of a case, for example through the contact support form's deflection tracking.

questions.prompt: Agents need to see order history stored in an ERP without copying it into Salesforce. What fits?

options.text: Asking customers to read out their order history
Salesforce Connect with external objects
A nightly import of every order into a custom object
Email-to-Case with the order history attached

questions.explanation: Salesforce Connect shows external data in real time as external objects, without storing copies.

questions.prompt: A client already has a telephony provider and wants a softphone inside Salesforce. What should be considered?

options.text: Replace every phone call with chat so no telephony integration is needed
A custom Call object that agents fill in by hand
Email-to-Case with call notes sent as emails
The provider's Open CTI integration or Service Cloud Voice

questions.explanation: Open CTI lets third-party telephony embed a softphone. Service Cloud Voice also supports partner telephony providers.

questions.prompt: When a case is closed, the billing system must issue a credit within seconds. What pattern fits?

options.text: A weekly CSV of closed cases sent to billing
An email to the billing team for each closed case
A nightly export of closed cases that billing processes the next morning
Publish a platform event or change event that billing subscribes to

questions.explanation: Event-driven integration delivers changes in near real time. Batch jobs can't meet a seconds-level requirement.

questions.prompt: Several back-end systems must be combined to answer a 'where is my order' request. What could simplify this?

options.text: Separate point-to-point Apex callouts from Salesforce to each back-end system
An integration layer such as MuleSoft exposing one API to Salesforce
Agents logging into each back-end system in turn
Copying all back-end data into Salesforce every hour

questions.explanation: An integration layer orchestrates calls to many systems and exposes a clean API, which reduces brittle point-to-point code.

questions.prompt: An Agentforce service agent needs live shipping status from a carrier's API. How is this usually exposed to the agent?

options.text: As an agent action, such as a flow or Apex that calls the API
Through a report that lists shipping statuses
By pasting the carrier's API documentation into the topic
Through a Knowledge article updated by the carrier

questions.explanation: Agent actions wrap flows, Apex or external services, so the agent can call the API with the right inputs and use the result.

questions.prompt: What is good practice for the user an integration authenticates as?

options.text: A dedicated integration user with only the permissions it needs
One shared login with full access, used by every integration in the org
The login of whichever agent set up the integration
One shared login with full access for every integration

questions.explanation: A dedicated, least-privilege integration user limits damage if credentials leak and keeps audit trails clear.
